clue.text: Plummy luwie caught mounting Grant

definitions.note: Simon Callow, the posh-voiced actor, is a luvvie, slang for a theatrical type

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
to grant is to allow; mounting says the caught letter sits on top in this down clue

explanation.surface: Private Eye innuendo: a posh actor caught in bed with Hugh Grant.
explanation.walkthrough: A luvvie is British slang for a gushing theatrical type; Simon Callow is a famously plummy-voiced English actor.
explanation.definitionFit: The actor Simon Callow, with his rich, plummy voice, is the archetypal theatrical luvvie.

clue.text: Congenital piss-artists? The Lords has its share of those!

definitions.meaning: first meaning, punning: people who pee (pee-ers) by birth, the two words sounding like inherited lords

definitions.text: The Lords has its share of those
definitions.meaning: second meaning: members of the House of Lords who sit by inherited title

explanation.walkthrough: A piss-artist is British slang for a drunk; here it is twisted into one who pees, so pee-ers. Hereditary peers sit in the House of Lords by birth.
explanation.definitionFit: Lords who inherited their seat by birth rather than appointment are a recognised class in Britain's upper chamber.

clue.text: Variety act with dog makes you flee!

parts.note: a turn is a performer's act in a variety show
to dog someone is to follow them, or tail them

explanation.surface: A music-hall dog act so bad the audience runs for the exits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dog' looks like the animal in the act; it is the verb to follow.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn tail is an idiom for running away from danger.

clue.text: Constitutional way to rob a drunk?

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
to roll someone is slang for robbing a drunk or sleeping person

explanation.surface: A question about whether mugging a drunk is lawful under the constitution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Constitutional' looks like an adjective about law; it is the noun for a health-giving walk.
explanation.definitionFit: A constitutional is an old-fashioned word for a leisurely walk taken for one's health.

clue.text: Dick's into genitalia on account of some backbencher's legislation

parts.note: a dick is a private detective, a private eye
members is a euphemism for male genitalia
a bill is an account for payment

explanation.surface: Private Eye smut: a detective is busy with private parts.
explanation.walkthrough: A Private Member's Bill is a law proposed in Parliament by a backbench MP rather than the government.
explanation.definitionFit: A private member's bill is draft legislation introduced by a backbench MP, not by a government minister.

clue.text: Blair first showing: Clare's last to leave

indicators.note: the letter is told to depart from the word for first showing

parts.note: a premiere is a film's or play's first showing

indicators.note: last asks for only the final letter of the name Clare

parts.note: final letter of Clare

explanation.surface: Tony Blair's first appearance, at which Clare Short is the last to walk out.
explanation.walkthrough: Clare Short was a minister who resigned from Blair's cabinet; here 'Clare's last' is just its final E, which 'to leave' drops from PREMIERE.
explanation.definitionFit: Tony Blair was the British Prime Minister, also called the Premier.

clue.text: Heaven on earth, though a tad untidy, Llangollen!

indicators.note: only a small portion of the following words is used, the answer sitting within them

parts.note: the letters run from the end of untidy into the start of Llangollen

explanation.surface: Praise for the Welsh town of Llangollen as paradise, if a little messy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a tad' says only a small piece of the next words is wanted: the answer runs from the end of 'untidy' into 'Llangollen', a small town in North Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: An idyll is a scene of perfect peace and happiness, a paradise in the world.

clue.text: Supports sexual partners

definitions.meaning: first meaning: frames or stands that hold something up
second meaning: those one ..., in the coarse sexual sense

explanation.walkthrough: Both senses come from the verb to mount: to set something on a backing, and to climb on top of a partner.
explanation.definitionFit: A mount is a backing or stand holding something up, and in slang it is also a person one has sex with.

clue.text: See 5
Poor Kylie, losing interest to live, all following the debut of Juliet Stevenson's character

indicators.note: the rest of the answer comes after the opening letter, so this piece follows it
a debut is a first appearance, so only the opening letter of Juliet is used

parts.note: first letter of Juliet

indicators.note: poor here means in bad shape, so the letters are put into a new order
Kylie loses one letter and takes on another in its place, the swap read as losing one thing to gain another

parts.note: I is the usual abbreviation for interest, as in rates
L stands for live, as on an electrical plug

explanation.surface: Actress Juliet Stevenson taking a role that leaves a poor Kylie Minogue lifeless.
explanation.walkthrough: Juliet Stevenson is a red herring: the character is Robert Louis Stevenson's. 'losing' swaps the interest letter for the live one, making KYLLE; 'Poor' jumbles that to EKYLL, and 'all following' sets it after 'the debut of' Juliet.
explanation.definitionFit: Dr Jekyll is the respectable half of Robert Louis Stevenson's Strange Case of Dr Jekyll and Mr Hyde.

clue.text: City editor (Scotsman) on speed

parts.note: MON is the stock Scots form of address, man
a ton is slang for a hundred miles an hour, a high speed

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor from Scotland, high on amphetamines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scotsman' and 'speed' suggest the newspaper and a drug; here MON is the Scots 'man' and TON is a hundred mph.
explanation.definitionFit: Edmonton is the capital of Alberta in Canada, and also a district of north London.

clue.text: See 5
Sort of farce that's representative of central government?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a style of British stage comedy named after the ... Theatre
second meaning: the London street of ministries, used as shorthand for the civil service

explanation.walkthrough: The Whitehall farces were trouser-dropping comedies staged at London's Whitehall Theatre; the question mark hints that government itself is a farce.
explanation.definitionFit: The street housing government ministries stands for the administration itself, and also names a genre of theatrical comedy.

clue.text: Rag promoting its owner's views undergoing re-location —- and a change of heart, possibly?

parts.note: a house newspaper or mouthpiece is called an organ
to transplant something is to move it to a new place

explanation.surface: A proprietor's newspaper moving offices and switching its editorial line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change of heart' usually means a change of opinion; read literally, a new heart is put in, and 'possibly' allows for other organs.
explanation.definitionFit: Replacing a diseased heart with a donor's one is a well-known surgical example of moving a body part between people.

clue.text: A devotee is to attach computer chip to ex-PM

indicators.note: the chip is joined to what follows

parts.note: to add is to attach one thing to another
IC is an integrated circuit, a chip
Ted Heath was a former British Prime Minister

explanation.surface: Instructions to wire a microchip into former Prime Minister Edward Heath.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a fill-in-the-blank: a devotee is addicted to whatever they adore. Ted is Edward Heath, PM 1970-74.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone devoted to a pastime is hooked on it, so the phrase completes as a fan being dependent on it.

clue.text: See 18
Big city virgin comes to town

parts.note: virgin means new, untouched
York is a cathedral town in northern England

explanation.surface: An innocent arriving in town from the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: York is the English cathedral city in North Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: New York is the largest US metropolis, nicknamed the Big Apple.

clue.text: PM heady, that is quite disoriented, by press overstatement

indicators.note: having lost all sense of direction, the letters are jumbled into a new order

parts.note: IE is the abbreviation of id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: A Prime Minister giddy with power and confused by newspaper exaggeration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quite disoriented' tells you to rearrange the letters of PM, HEADY and IE.
explanation.definitionFit: Hype is exaggerated publicity, and coverage blown up by newspapers and broadcasters is called media hype.

clue.text: Night fliers inhaling nitrogen to induce periods

indicators.note: breathing in, so the gas goes inside the insects

parts.note: moths are insects that fly at night
N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen

explanation.surface: Moths breathing in a gas that brings on menstruation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inhaling' puts N inside MOTHS. 'periods' suggests menstruation, the surface's sense; the answer is periods of time.
explanation.definitionFit: Months are periods of time on the calendar, each roughly four weeks long.

clue.text: Implants causing those people commonly to have rows

parts.note: 'em is the casual spoken form of them
garden beds are planted in rows

explanation.walkthrough: 'rows' suggests quarrels; it is the rows of a garden bed.
explanation.definitionFit: To embed something is to set it firmly into a surrounding mass, as an implant is set.

clue.text: State involved in fellatio watch

indicators.note: the answer is caught up inside the run of letters of the next two words

parts.note: the letters straddle the end of fellatio and the start of watch

explanation.surface: A sexual act carried out while someone keeps watch, or a nation caught up in a scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved in' signals the answer is tucked inside the clue: it straddles the end of 'fellatio' and the start of 'watch'.
explanation.definitionFit: Iowa is one of the fifty United States, in the Midwest.

clue.text: Saucy Eye feature: 'Ten nameless men Horatio screwed'

indicators.note: screwed in its sense of twisted or messed up, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the number ten as written

explanation.surface: A cheeky magazine headline about Horatio Nelson and ten anonymous men.
explanation.walkthrough: TEN without N leaves TE; TE + MEN + HORATIO rearranged gives the answer. N is a dictionary abbreviation for name.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a gossip column in Private Eye about the goings-on among MPs at Westminster.

clue.text: Adore, after one 'E' and some cocaine, a story

indicators.note: the word for adore comes after the other pieces

parts.note: an means one, as in an apple
C is slang shorthand for cocaine
to dote on someone is to adore them

explanation.surface: A clubber's confession of loving everyone after an ecstasy tablet and a line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'E' looks like ecstasy and is simply the letter; C is street slang for cocaine, and 'after' sends the word for adore to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: An anecdote is a short personal tale told as an amusing account.

clue.text: Willinspired character, a complete arse

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the weaver Nick ... in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream, Will being Shakespeare
second meaning: another word for the backside

explanation.walkthrough: 'Willinspired' is Will-inspired: created by Will Shakespeare. Bottom in the play is turned into an ass, which makes the second half a double joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's comic weaver shares his name with the buttocks, and an arse is British slang for both the backside and a fool.

clue.text: British brand of imperturbability? Makes you spit!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: calm self-possession, the stiff upper lip thought typically British
second meaning: the mucus coughed up from the throat

explanation.walkthrough: The same word means unflappable composure and catarrh that a cold brings up.
explanation.definitionFit: Coolness under pressure is called phlegm, from the old humour thought to cause calm, and the throat mucus you cough up has the same name.

clue.text: Sun-smitten, uneducated white reactionary?

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read literally: a neck turned red by the sun
second meaning: a poor white rural American, bigoted and conservative

explanation.walkthrough: The insult comes from farm labourers whose necks were burnt red working in the fields; the first half reads the word literally.
explanation.definitionFit: The American slur names a rural working-class white person seen as ignorant and politically backward.
